title: A fixed release site limits dust absorption to arcsin(epsilon)/pi for directly lit escaping grains
abstract: We test the sky area that dust from one fixed collision site can fill. All launch velocities are within epsilon times the circular speed of the same reference velocity. For a point star, central motion and constant radiation-force ratios beta >= 0.70, we prove that the absorbed stellar fraction is at most arcsin(epsilon)/pi when epsilon < 0.2254. The bound permits any source age and supply rate. It uses orbital-plane conservation and an escape asymptote before the opposite radial direction. For the prior Gaia20cdd model absorption range of 0.009-0.034, epsilon must be at least 0.0283-0.1066. At 4 au this requires maximum launch changes of at least 0.38-1.42 km/s for a 0.80-solar-mass star, or 0.55-2.07 km/s for a 1.70-solar-mass close binary. This is a necessary condition on a velocity maximum, not a velocity dispersion or an impact detection. Gas, force shielding, a moving source, finite stellar size and an uncertain bolometric dust luminosity limit the application. We give the proof, original code, model tables, a figure, solid-angle quadrature and 288 independent Cartesian orbit checks. No survey records or external raw data are bundled.
